claim: Insulin secretion from β-cells is reduced at the onset of type-1 diabetes.
source: Insulin secretion from β-cells is reduced at the onset of type-1 and during type-2 diabetes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about diabetes pathology.

claim: Insulin secretion from β-cells is reduced during type-2 diabetes.
source: Insulin secretion from β-cells is reduced at the onset of type-1 and during type-2 diabetes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about diabetes pathology.

claim: Two subpopulations of insulin granules exist with different calcium affinities.
source: We show that this behavior is correlated with two subpopulations of insulin granules whose relative abundance is differentially shifted depending on diabetic model condition.
evidence: The abstract states this finding based on the study's functional analyses.

claim: The two types of insulin granules have different release characteristics.
source: The two types of granules have different release characteristics, distinct lipid and protein compositions, and package different secretory contents alongside insulin.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: The two types of insulin granules have distinct lipid compositions.
source: The two types of granules have different release characteristics, distinct lipid and protein compositions, and package different secretory contents alongside insulin.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: The two types of insulin granules have distinct protein compositions.
source: The two types of granules have different release characteristics, distinct lipid and protein compositions, and package different secretory contents alongside insulin.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: The two types of insulin granules package different secretory contents alongside insulin.
source: The two types of granules have different release characteristics, distinct lipid and protein compositions, and package different secretory contents alongside insulin.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: Blood glucose levels are maintained in a narrow range by secretion of insulin from pancreatic β-cells.
source: Blood glucose levels are maintained in a narrow range by secretion of the hormone insulin from pancreatic β-cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established physiological knowledge.

claim: Insufficient insulin secretion leads to elevated levels of blood glucose resulting in diabetes.
source: Insufficient insulin secretion leads to elevated levels of blood glucose resulting in diabetes (Rorsman and Ashcroft, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Type 1 diabetes results primarily from immune-mediated killing of pancreatic β-cells.
source: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) results primarily from immune-mediated killing of pancreatic β-cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about T1D etiology.

claim: Type 2 diabetes arises when peripheral resistance to insulin signaling causes persistent demand for insulin secretion and eventual β-cell exhaustion.
source: In contrast, type 2 diabetes (T2D) arises when peripheral resistance to insulin signaling causes persistent demand for insulin secretion and eventual β-cell exhaustion (Guthrie and Guthrie, 2004; Rorsman and Ashcroft, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Secretory defects have been observed in diabetic human islet cells.
source: Secretory defects have been observed in diabetic human islet cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an observation from prior research.

claim: Treatment with proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α, INF-γ, and IL-1β models the onset of T1D.
source: Onset of T1D is modeled by treatment of insulin-secreting cells with proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α, INF-γ, and IL-1β, which leads to decreased insulin release and a loss of Doc2B, an established biomarker for the disease (Aslamy et al., 2018a; Aslamy et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the modeling approach.

claim: Cytokine treatment leads to decreased insulin release and a loss of Doc2B.
source: Onset of T1D is modeled by treatment of insulin-secreting cells with proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α, INF-γ, and IL-1β, which leads to decreased insulin release and a loss of Doc2B, an established biomarker for the disease (Aslamy et al., 2018a; Aslamy et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Doc2B is an established biomarker for type 1 diabetes.
source: Onset of T1D is modeled by treatment of insulin-secreting cells with proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α, INF-γ, and IL-1β, which leads to decreased insulin release and a loss of Doc2B, an established biomarker for the disease (Aslamy et al., 2018a; Aslamy et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: T2D is associated with extended exposure to elevated free fatty acids caused by high fat diets.
source: T2D is associated with extended exposure to elevated free fatty acids (FFA) caused by high fat diets (Grill and Qvigstad, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the association.

claim: Sustained treatment of insulin-secreting cells with palmitate models the lipotoxicity component of T2D.
source: The lipotoxicity component of T2D is frequently modeled by sustained treatment of insulin-secreting cells with palmitate, resulting in reduced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (Hoppa et al., 2009; Sako and Grill, 1990).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the modeling approach.

claim: Palmitate treatment results in reduced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.
source: The lipotoxicity component of T2D is frequently modeled by sustained treatment of insulin-secreting cells with palmitate, resulting in reduced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (Hoppa et al., 2009; Sako and Grill, 1990).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Stimulated secretion of insulin normally occurs in two sequential phases: an acute first phase and a sustained second phase.
source: Stimulated secretion of insulin normally occurs in two sequential phases, an acute first phase and a sustained second phase, which are differently affected in the T1D and T2D models.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about insulin secretion.

claim: Cytokine treatment primarily suppresses the second phase of insulin secretion.
source: Modeling the inflammation of T1D by cytokine treatment causes a defect in insulin secretion attributed to the loss of Doc2B (Aslamy et al., 2018a; Aslamy et al., 2018b), which primarily suppresses the second phase of secretion (Ramalingam et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Palmitate treatment strongly decreases the first phase of insulin secretion.
source: Conversely, modeling T2D by palmitate treatment strongly decreases the first phase (Rorsman and Ashcroft, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: Granules purified from untreated cells exhibit a biphasic calcium response.
source: Quantification of fusion as a function of calcium concentration revealed a biphasic response with granules purified from untreated cells (Figure 1B, green, control).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Granules purified from palmitate-treated cells exhibited a monophasic high-affinity calcium response with K1/2 = 12 ± 2 µM.
source: Granules purified from cells following a 72 hr treatment with palmitate (delivered as a BSA complex and used to model elevated free fatty acid [FFA] observed during T2D Rorsman and Ashcroft, 2018) exhibited a monophasic high-affinity calcium response (K1/2 = 12 ± 2 µM, Figure 1B, blue).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with specific quantitative data and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Granules purified from cytokine-treated cells showed a shift to a low-affinity monophasic response with K1/2 = 41 ± 4 µM.
source: In contrast, granules purified from cells following a 20 hr treatment with cytokines TNF-α, INF-γ, and IL-1β that model the inflammation associated with the onset of T1D (Aslamy et al., 2018a; Aslamy et al., 2018b) showed a shift to a low-affinity monophasic response (K1/2 = 41 ± 4 µM, Figure 1B, red).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with specific quantitative data and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Overexpression of Doc2B prior to cytokine treatment prevented the shift of the calcium dose-response.
source: Overexpression of Doc2B prior to cytokine treatment, which had previously been shown to reverse cytokine effects on β-cells (Aslamy et al., 2018b), prevented the shift of the calcium dose-response (Figure 1C, purple).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 1C and a citation.

claim: Granules purified from palmitate-treated cells exhibited only slow release modes at 100 μM calcium.
source: Granules purified following diabetic model treatments exhibited only slow release modes from palmitate-treated cells and only fast release modes from cytokine-treated cells when fusion was assayed at 100 μM calcium (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 1F showing the data.

claim: Granules purified from cytokine-treated cells exhibited only fast release modes at 100 μM calcium.
source: Granules purified following diabetic model treatments exhibited only slow release modes from palmitate-treated cells and only fast release modes from cytokine-treated cells when fusion was assayed at 100 μM calcium (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 1F showing the data.

claim: Overexpression of Doc2B restored the slow release mode of granules purified from cytokine-treated cells.
source: Overexpression of Doc2B restored the slow release mode of granules purified from cytokine-treated cells (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 1F showing the data.

claim: Increased depolarization decreased the duration of C-peptide release events from intact cells.
source: Increased depolarization, which increased calcium influx (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), decreased the duration of C-peptide release events from intact cells (Figure 2B and C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C) corresponding to fast and slow fusion events observed in the reconstitution assay (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with references to multiple figures showing the data.

claim: Palmitate treatment increased release duration in intact cells.
source: At both high and low stimulation strengths, palmitate treatment increased release duration whereas cytokine treatment decreased release duration (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) corresponding to the shifts in release modes observed in the reconstitution assay (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with references to figures showing the data.

claim: Cytokine treatment decreased release duration in intact cells.
source: At both high and low stimulation strengths, palmitate treatment increased release duration whereas cytokine treatment decreased release duration (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) corresponding to the shifts in release modes observed in the reconstitution assay (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with references to figures showing the data.

claim: Granules purified from untreated cells had a diameter of 195 ± 61 nm as measured by cryo-EM.
source: Granules had a diameter of 195 ± 61 nm when purified from untreated cells, 173 ± 43 nm when purified from palmitate-treated cells, and 222 ± 53 nm when purified from cytokine-treated cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with specific quantitative measurements from cryo-EM.

claim: Granules purified from palmitate-treated cells had a diameter of 173 ± 43 nm as measured by cryo-EM.
source: Granules had a diameter of 195 ± 61 nm when purified from untreated cells, 173 ± 43 nm when purified from palmitate-treated cells, and 222 ± 53 nm when purified from cytokine-treated cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with specific quantitative measurements from cryo-EM.

claim: Granules purified from cytokine-treated cells had a diameter of 222 ± 53 nm as measured by cryo-EM.
source: Granules had a diameter of 195 ± 61 nm when purified from untreated cells, 173 ± 43 nm when purified from palmitate-treated cells, and 222 ± 53 nm when purified from cytokine-treated cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with specific quantitative measurements from cryo-EM.

claim: Overexpression of Doc2B shifted the size distribution of purified granules back to 191 ± 37 nm.
source: Overexpression of Doc2B shifted the size distribution of purified granules back to 191 ± 37 nm.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with specific quantitative measurements from cryo-EM.

claim: FCS measurements confirmed granule diameters of 194 ± 11 nm for untreated cells.
source: The shifts in granule size were confirmed using fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) to measure the hydrodynamic radii of the C-peptide-GFP containing granules with diameters of 194 ± 11 nm, 183 ± 4 nm, 220 ± 2 nm, and 187 ± 3 nm for granules from untreated, palmitate-treated, cytokine-treated, and Doc2B-protected cytokine-treated cells, respectively (Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with specific quantitative measurements from FCS and reference to figures.

claim: FCS measurements confirmed granule diameters of 183 ± 4 nm for palmitate-treated cells.
source: The shifts in granule size were confirmed using fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) to measure the hydrodynamic radii of the C-peptide-GFP containing granules with diameters of 194 ± 11 nm, 183 ± 4 nm, 220 ± 2 nm, and 187 ± 3 nm for granules from untreated, palmitate-treated, cytokine-treated, and Doc2B-protected cytokine-treated cells, respectively (Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with specific quantitative measurements from FCS and reference to figures.

claim: FCS measurements confirmed granule diameters of 220 ± 2 nm for cytokine-treated cells.
source: The shifts in granule size were confirmed using fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) to measure the hydrodynamic radii of the C-peptide-GFP containing granules with diameters of 194 ± 11 nm, 183 ± 4 nm, 220 ± 2 nm, and 187 ± 3 nm for granules from untreated, palmitate-treated, cytokine-treated, and Doc2B-protected cytokine-treated cells, respectively (Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with specific quantitative measurements from FCS and reference to figures.

claim: FCS measurements confirmed granule diameters of 187 ± 3 nm for Doc2B-protected cytokine-treated cells.
source: The shifts in granule size were confirmed using fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) to measure the hydrodynamic radii of the C-peptide-GFP containing granules with diameters of 194 ± 11 nm, 183 ± 4 nm, 220 ± 2 nm, and 187 ± 3 nm for granules from untreated, palmitate-treated, cytokine-treated, and Doc2B-protected cytokine-treated cells, respectively (Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with specific quantitative measurements from FCS and reference to figures.

claim: Two distinct subpopulations of insulin granules exist: larger fast releasing granules susceptible to palmitate treatment and smaller slow releasing granules susceptible to cytokine treatment.
source: In combination, the data on calcium affinity, release modes, and granule size are consistent with the presence of two distinct subpopulations of insulin granules: larger fast releasing granules that are susceptible to palmitate T2D-mimicking treatment and smaller slow releasing granules that are susceptible to cytokine T1D-mimicking treatment.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of data.

claim: Synaptotagmin is the calcium sensor for exocytosis.
source: The calcium sensor for exocytosis is synaptotagmin (syt), a granule membrane-associated protein with two C2 domains (Brose et al., 1992) that promotes assembly of the SNARE complex and catalyzes fusion between the granule and plasma membranes (Jahn and Fasshauer, 2012), leading to the release of insulin from the cell.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Syt7 and syt9 are the two predominant isoforms relevant for insulin secretion.
source: Syt7 and syt9 are the two predominant isoforms relevant for insulin secretion (Gustavsson et al., 2008; Iezzi et al., 2005), with syt7 and syt9 known to have a high and low affinity for calcium, respectively (Zhang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Syt7 has a high affinity for calcium.
source: Syt7 and syt9 are the two predominant isoforms relevant for insulin secretion (Gustavsson et al., 2008; Iezzi et al., 2005), with syt7 and syt9 known to have a high and low affinity for calcium, respectively (Zhang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: Syt9 has a low affinity for calcium.
source: Syt7 and syt9 are the two predominant isoforms relevant for insulin secretion (Gustavsson et al., 2008; Iezzi et al., 2005), with syt7 and syt9 known to have a high and low affinity for calcium, respectively (Zhang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: The levels of syt7 and syt9 were unaffected in cell lysates after palmitate or cytokine treatment.
source: The levels of both of these isoforms were unaffected in cell lysates after palmitate or cytokine treatment (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3A and B showing the data.

claim: Treatments with cytokines or palmitate caused distinct and different shifts in syt isoform distribution in fractionated cell lysates.
source: However, fractionation of cell lysates by density gradient centrifugation revealed that treatments of cells with T1D-mimicking cytokines or T2D-mimicking palmitate caused distinct and different shifts in syt isoform distribution (Figure 3A and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3A and C showing the data.

claim: Granules from palmitate-treated cells show a loss of syt9 while still containing syt7.
source: Granules from palmitate-treated cells show a loss of the lower affinity syt9 while still containing the high-affinity calcium sensor syt7.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an observation from the fractionation data.

claim: Granules from cytokine-treated cells show a loss of syt7 while still containing syt9.
source: Conversely, granules from cytokine-treated cells show a loss of syt7 while still containing syt9 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3C showing the data.

claim: Doc2B protected the redistribution of syt7 from fraction 9 of cytokine-treated cells.
source: Doc2B protected the redistribution of syt7 from fraction 9 of cytokine-treated cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3C showing the data.

claim: Syt7 and syt9 reside on separate subpopulations of insulin granules.
source: Immunodepletion of intact granules from untreated cells using antibodies against either syt7 or syt9 revealed that these two isoforms reside on separate subpopulations of insulin granules (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3D showing the immunodepletion data.

claim: Residual syt7 granules (after syt9 depletion) had diameters of 168 ± 36 nm by cryo-EM and 185 ± 4 nm by FCS.
source: Residual syt7 granules (after syt9 depletion) had diameters of 168 ± 36 nm (cryo-EM) and 185 ± 4 nm (FCS), whereas residual syt9 granules (after syt7 immunodepletion) were 211 ± 46 nm (cryo-EM) and 197 ± 7 nm (FCS) (Figure 3E and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with specific quantitative measurements and references to figures.

claim: Residual syt9 granules (after syt7 immunodepletion) had diameters of 211 ± 46 nm by cryo-EM and 197 ± 7 nm by FCS.
source: Residual syt7 granules (after syt9 depletion) had diameters of 168 ± 36 nm (cryo-EM) and 185 ± 4 nm (FCS), whereas residual syt9 granules (after syt7 immunodepletion) were 211 ± 46 nm (cryo-EM) and 197 ± 7 nm (FCS) (Figure 3E and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with specific quantitative measurements and references to figures.

claim: Syt7 granules have a calcium dose response with K1/2 = 10 ± 1 µM.
source: The dose response to calcium was monophasic with a K1/2 = 10 ± 1 µM for syt7 granules (depleted of syt9) and monophasic with a K1/2 = 48 ± 3 µM for syt9 granules (depleted for syt7, Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with specific quantitative data and reference to Figure 3F.

claim: Syt9 granules have a calcium dose response with K1/2 = 48 ± 3 µM.
source: The dose response to calcium was monophasic with a K1/2 = 10 ± 1 µM for syt7 granules (depleted of syt9) and monophasic with a K1/2 = 48 ± 3 µM for syt9 granules (depleted for syt7, Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with specific quantitative data and reference to Figure 3F.

claim: The syt isoform defines the release mode, with syt7 granules releasing contents more slowly than syt9 granules.
source: Analysis of the modes of C-peptide-GFP release obtained from individual fusion events in the planar membrane fusion assay showed that the syt isoform also defines the release mode, with the syt7 granules releasing contents more slowly than the syt9 granules (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with references to figures showing the data.

claim: T1D-mimicking cytokine treatment results in loss of syt7 granules.
source: The similarity in shifts of calcium affinity, release mode, and size distribution lead us to conclude that T1D-mimicking cytokine treatment results in loss of syt7 granules, whereas T2D-mimicking palmitate treatment results in loss of syt9 granules.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of data.

claim: T2D-mimicking palmitate treatment results in loss of syt9 granules.
source: The similarity in shifts of calcium affinity, release mode, and size distribution lead us to conclude that T1D-mimicking cytokine treatment results in loss of syt7 granules, whereas T2D-mimicking palmitate treatment results in loss of syt9 granules.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of data.

claim: Syt7 granules are substantially enriched in cholesterol compared to unseparated control granules.
source: Strikingly, syt7 granules were substantially enriched in both cholesterol and sphingomyelin compared to unseparated control granules, while syt9 granules contained much less of both lipid species (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 4A showing the data.

claim: Syt7 granules are substantially enriched in sphingomyelin compared to unseparated control granules.
source: Strikingly, syt7 granules were substantially enriched in both cholesterol and sphingomyelin compared to unseparated control granules, while syt9 granules contained much less of both lipid species (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 4A showing the data.

claim: Syt9 granules contained much less cholesterol and sphingomyelin compared to control granules.
source: Strikingly, syt7 granules were substantially enriched in both cholesterol and sphingomyelin compared to unseparated control granules, while syt9 granules contained much less of both lipid species (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 4A showing the data.

claim: The SM-Kate signal predominantly colocalized with the GFP signal while there were numerous GFP-positive puncta that lacked the SM-Kate signal.
source: The EQ-SM-Kate signal predominantly colocalized with the GFP signal while there were numerous GFP-positive puncta that lacked the EQ-SM-Kate signal (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 4D and E showing the microscopy data.

claim: EQ-sol-GFP broadly labels vesicles in the secretory pathway while the SM-Kate sensor selectively labels organelles/granules enriched in sphingomyelin.
source: This indicates that EQ-sol-GFP broadly labels vesicles in the secretory pathway while the SM-Kate sensor selectively labels organelles/granules enriched in sphingomyelin.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the colocalization data.

claim: Sphingomyelin 42:1 is 3-fold enriched in syt7 compared to syt9 granules.
source: When sphingomyelin 42:1, which likely contains the two predominant sphingomyelin tails, 18:0 in the sphingosine and 24:1 in the acyl chain positions (O'Brien and Rouser, 1964), is visualized in a bar graph and compared to all other pooled lipid species in each headgroup class, it is apparent that sphingomyelin 42:1 is 3-fold enriched in syt7 compared to syt9 granules (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 4G showing the mass spectrometry data.

claim: No other lipid classes show any significant enrichment in either type of granule.
source: None of the other lipid classes and not even other sphingomyelin species show any significant enrichment in either type of granule.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a finding from the mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: Syt7 but not syt9 was palmitoylated.
source: Subsequent immunoprecipitation with anti-syt antibodies revealed that syt7 but not syt9 was palmitoylated (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5A showing the palmitoylation assay data.

claim: Palmitoylation of syt7 likely explains the selective association of syt7 with sphingomyelin- and cholesterol-rich granules.
source: This likely explains the selective association of syt7 with sphingomyelin- and cholesterol-rich granules.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the palmitoylation data.

claim: VAMP7 was significantly enriched in syt7 granules.
source: VAMP2, VAMP3, VAMP4, and VAMP8 were found in roughly equal amounts in both syt7 and syt9 granules, whereas VAMP7 was significantly enriched in syt7 granules (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5B showing the western blot quantification.

claim: CAPS2 was enriched on syt9 granules.
source: CAPS2 was found to be enriched on syt-9 granules, while Doc2B was enriched on syt7 granules (Figure 5B), indicating that the fusion regulatory machinery differs in part between the granule subpopulations.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5B showing the western blot quantification.

claim: Doc2B was enriched on syt7 granules.
source: CAPS2 was found to be enriched on syt-9 granules, while Doc2B was enriched on syt7 granules (Figure 5B), indicating that the fusion regulatory machinery differs in part between the granule subpopulations.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5B showing the western blot quantification.

claim: MIF, IGF2, and IAPP are detected in syt7 granules.
source: MIF, IGF2, and IAPP are detected in syt7 granules while NPY is predominantly detected in syt9 granules (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5B showing the western blot data.

claim: NPY is predominantly detected in syt9 granules.
source: MIF, IGF2, and IAPP are detected in syt7 granules while NPY is predominantly detected in syt9 granules (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5B showing the western blot data.

claim: PC2 was markedly enriched in syt7 granules.
source: PC1/3 was equally distributed between the two granule subpopulations, while PC2 was markedly enriched in syt7 granules (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5B showing the western blot data.

claim: VGLUT1 is present only in syt9 granules.
source: VGLUT1 is present only in syt9 granules, whereas VNUT and VGAT are present only in syt7 granules (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5B showing the western blot data.

claim: VNUT and VGAT are present only in syt7 granules.
source: VGLUT1 is present only in syt9 granules, whereas VNUT and VGAT are present only in syt7 granules (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5B showing the western blot data.

claim: VMAT2 is equally distributed between the two subpopulations of granules.
source: VMAT2 is equally distributed between the two subpopulations of granules.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a finding from the western blot analysis.

claim: Untreated GRINCH cells secreted C-peptide-GFP in increasing amounts as the depolarization strength was increased.
source: Untreated GRINCH cells secreted C-peptide-GFP in increasing amounts as the depolarization strength was increased, consistent with its presence in both granule subpopulations (Figure 6A, top panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 6A showing the secretion data.

claim: ATP secretion measured with INS 832/13 cells was maximal at 25 mM KCl.
source: ATP secretion measured with INS 832/13 cells was maximal at 25 mM KCl, consistent with its selective concentration in syt7 granules.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a finding from the ATP secretion assay.

claim: Glutamate secretion from INS 832/13 cells was only detected at 90 mM KCl.
source: In contrast, glutamate secretion from INS 832/13 cells was only detected at 90 mM KCl, consistent with its selective concentration in syt9 granules (also see Figure 6—figure supplement 1, for calibrations and absolute amounts of secretion under different conditions).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: For palmitate-treated cells, C-peptide-GFP secretion was stimulated at 25 mM KCl and the response was not further increased at 90 mM KCl.
source: For palmitate-treated cells, C-peptide-GFP secretion was stimulated at 25 mM KCl and the response was not further increased at 90 mM KCl.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a finding from the secretion assay.

claim: Palmitate had no observable effect on the secretion of ATP.
source: Palmitate also had no observable effect on the secretion of ATP, but drastically reduced the secretion of glutamate (Figure 6A, middle panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 6A showing the secretion data.

claim: Palmitate drastically reduced the secretion of glutamate.
source: Palmitate also had no observable effect on the secretion of ATP, but drastically reduced the secretion of glutamate (Figure 6A, middle panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 6A showing the secretion data.

claim: Cytokine treatment reduced the secretion of C-peptide-GFP, especially upon mild stimulation.
source: By contrast, the cytokine treatment reduced the secretion of C-peptide-GFP (especially upon mild stimulation) and significantly decreased the secretion of ATP, while secretion of glutamate was not much altered as compared to untreated cells (Figure 6A, bottom panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 6A showing the secretion data.

claim: Cytokine treatment significantly decreased the secretion of ATP.
source: By contrast, the cytokine treatment reduced the secretion of C-peptide-GFP (especially upon mild stimulation) and significantly decreased the secretion of ATP, while secretion of glutamate was not much altered as compared to untreated cells (Figure 6A, bottom panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 6A showing the secretion data.

claim: Cytokine treatment did not much alter secretion of glutamate as compared to untreated cells.
source: By contrast, the cytokine treatment reduced the secretion of C-peptide-GFP (especially upon mild stimulation) and significantly decreased the secretion of ATP, while secretion of glutamate was not much altered as compared to untreated cells (Figure 6A, bottom panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 6A showing the secretion data.

claim: Insulin granules can no longer be considered generic storage units for releasing the full range of secretory molecules without regard to timing and signal strength.
source: Therefore, insulin granules can no longer be considered generic storage units for releasing the full range of secretory molecules without regard to timing and signal strength.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: The biphasic secretory pattern of insulin release can be interpreted as a staged release of selected peptides and transmitters over time and levels of intracellular calcium.
source: Because the granule subpopulations with secretory cargo compositions have different calcium affinities furnished by different synaptotagmin isoforms (Figure 3), we propose that these phases can be interpreted as a staged release of selected peptides and transmitters over time and levels of intracellular calcium.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a proposal based on the study's findings.

claim: Syt9 granules release their content primarily in the first phase of secretion during the initial spike in intracellular calcium.
source: In our new model linking the progression of T1D and T2D to different subpopulations of insulin secretory granules in the same cells, we posit that the syt9 granules release their content primarily in the first phase of secretion during the initial spike in intracellular calcium supported by their close proximity to calcium channels (Hoppa et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a model proposed by the authors with a citation.

claim: Granules harboring syt7 would release their content during both phases of insulin secretion.
